notebooks.summary: Recent findings identify algebraic conditions for identifying irreducible autocatalytic subnetworks within stoichiometric matrices and demonstrate programmable, history-dependent chemical responses in flow-controlled reaction systems.

detail.title: Experimental Foundations of Autocatalytic Chemical Memory
detail.summary: Recent findings identify algebraic conditions for identifying irreducible autocatalytic subnetworks within stoichiometric matrices and demonstrate programmable, history-dependent chemical responses in flow-controlled reaction systems.
detail.findings:
Algebraic conditions on submatrices of the stoichiometric matrix S allow for the identification of irreducible autocatalytic subnetworks. [peer-0592c13110957d2468eeda39] [peer-a2fc78f9c0fb4e42f8cc3e12]

Trypsin-catalyzed reaction networks under flow conditions can be programmed to exhibit history-dependent, neuromorphic responses. [peer-756d5cf5076d5b4a00b1070b]
detail.limitations: The current findings rely on specific flow-reactor conditions to sustain non-equilibrium persistence; the transition from programmable input to autonomous, persistent memory in complex, uncontrolled environments remains a distinct theoretical and experimental gap.
detail.next_questions: Can these programmable history-dependent responses be reconfigured into autonomously stable memory states without continuous flow control, and how do they scale within more complex metabolic networks?
detail.reason: Incorporating new stoichiometric network analysis and experimental flow-reactor evidence to advance the project on autocatalytic chemical memory.
